title: Equal finite stalk bases on a Koszul-regular chart
statement: Let i:Z→Y be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion], V an open of Z, z a point of V, and n,m natural numbers. Let U be an affine open of Y containing i(z), with section ring A, and let f:Fin m→A be a Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence] generating the kernel ideal [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] on U. Let B=i_*O_Z, G=H^n(RHom_Y(B,B)) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pur-derived-internal-hom], T=(i*G)|V [def-pc-module-pullback], and E=exteriorSheaf(Hom_Z(i*ker(i),O_Z)|V,n) [def-pur-sheaf-hom, def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. Each of T_z and E_z [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] has a basis over O_{V,z} indexed by the n-element subsets of Fin m. No map between these two stalks or compatibility of these bases is asserted; regularity is required only on U.

source.place: Lemma 48.15.4, contraction products and zero-differential Hom calculation; Tag 0BQW, degree-one boundary

proof.text: Use the local self Ext pullback frame on i^{-1}(U). Restrict this frame along V by composition of open restrictions and the over-site/free-sheaf equivalence. The local coordinate projections and inclusions induce linear maps on the stalk at z. Their finite sum is the identity and their pairwise composites are Kronecker deltas, so these maps are mutually inverse to the finite coordinate module over O_{V,z}. Transport its standard basis and reindex ULift to obtain the first basis.

Use the Koszul conormal basis and the affine conormal frame. Restriction of internal Hom to the over site, its contravariant action on the conormal frame, and finite-free duality give a dual frame of the same rank on i^{-1}(U). Restrict this frame to V on the inverse image of that open. The exterior local-free comparison gives a frame indexed by the increasing n-element subsets. Apply the explicit stalk-coordinate equivalence to this frame at z, transport the product basis and reindex ULift. Empty index types and degree zero use the same finite coordinate identities.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 48.15.4, plus Tags 062I and 01R3; Y2 completed the conormal dual/exterior frame and both finite coordinate stalk transports in Lean, leaving only the affine derived chart frame. K5 retirement, 2026-10-20: retain the same proof and transport the official comparison along the proved exterior-construction equalities. Q8 retirement, 2026-10-21: the source-library theorem preserves both finite-coordinate arguments; compatibility with the legacy exteriorSheaf formulation is proved in each consumer using exteriorSheaf_eq_exteriorPower.

lean.statement:
theorem koszulRegularImmersion_self_ext_stalk_bases
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (V : Z.Opens) (n : ℕ)
    (z : V.toScheme) (U : Y.affineOpens) (hzU : i z.1 ∈ U.1)
    (m : ℕ) (f : Fin m → Γ(Y, U.1))
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = i.ker.ideal U)
    (hreg : RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular f) :
    let B := (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf)
    let S := DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0
    let H := derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) Y.toRingedSpace.sheaf
    let G := (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) (n : ℤ)).obj
        (H.obj (op (S.obj B), S.obj B))
    let T := (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj
      ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj G)
    let E := Scheme.Modules.exteriorPower
      ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj
        (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := Z.sheaf)
          ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj i.ker.toModules)
          (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf))) n
    Nonempty (Module.Basis (Set.powersetCard (Fin m) n)
      (V.toScheme.presheaf.stalk z) (T.presheaf.stalk z)) ∧
    Nonempty (Module.Basis (Set.powersetCard (Fin m) n)
      (V.toScheme.presheaf.stalk z) (E.presheaf.stalk z))
